findings.title: V2 canManage() (no-arg) treats VIEW scope as sufficient for MANAGE operations
findings.body: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() (lines 64-71) the body returns true if hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE) holds. That call lets any caller with the VIEW scope on the all-groups resource pass the check. Operations that gate on the no-arg canManage (e.g. GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup -> requireManage()) will then allow callers to create/modify/delete groups even though they only have view permission. The interface JavaDoc on GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage() codifies this as the intended V2 behavior, but it is an explicit regression relative to V1 (GroupPermissions.canManage() is gated strictly on the MANAGE_USERS admin role) and the testViewGroups test grants Set.of(VIEW) yet does not assert that group management remains denied, so the regression is not caught. A maintainer should confirm whether 'VIEW implies MANAGE on groups' is really desired.

findings.title: Possible NullPointerException when getResourceTypeResource returns null
findings.body: In the private hasPermission(String groupId, String... scopes) method (around line 144), when the per-group resource lookup returns null the code falls back to AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and immediately calls policyStore.findByResource(server, resource).isEmpty(). AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource() explicitly can return null (when supportsAuthorizationSchema is false, when the resourceType is unknown, or when the all-groups resource has not been created yet). Passing null to policyStore.findByResource(...) is not null-guarded and throws NPE in the JPA implementation. Because canView() (no-arg) and canManage() (no-arg) both call hasPermission(null, ...) for any caller without MANAGE_USERS, this NPE can be hit during normal V2 permission evaluation whenever the GROUPS type resource has not been created.

findings.title: Same NPE risk in UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission when the all-users resource is missing
findings.body: The private hasPermission(UserModel, EvaluationContext, String...) method has the same structure: when the specific user resource is missing it calls AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, AdminPermissionsSchema.USERS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and then policyStore.findByResource(server, resource).isEmpty() without a null check. When the USERS type resource does not exist (resourceTypeResource returns null) this will pass null to policyStore.findByResource and raise NPE. Every canView/canManage/canImpersonate/canMapRoles/canManageGroupMembership path can trigger this, so the risk surface is large.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission stores Resource DB IDs instead of group IDs
findings.body: Inside the lambda passed to resourceStore.findByType(...) (around line 121) the code uses groupResource.getId() both as the argument to hasPermission and as the value added to the granted set. The Resource model's id is the database primary key (a UUID), but hasPermission does resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId) (lookup by name, not by id) and the all-V2 group resources are named with the group id (see AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup which returns group.getId()). A UUID never matches a resource name, so hasPermission always falls through to the all-groups fallback for every individual group, and the granted set is filled with Resource DB UUIDs rather than group ids. As soon as a caller only has the all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS / MANAGE_MEMBERS permission (no per-group grants), getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns a non-empty set of UUIDs that no real group matches, UsersResource.searchForUserStream filters by these bogus ids and returns zero users even though the caller should see members of every group. The bug is latent because the test scenarios always grant per-group permissions (so the fallback policyStore.isEmpty() short-circuits to false and the granted set stays empty), but in production this manifests as 'admin has all-groups permission yet sees no users'.

findings.title: getResourceName is not taught the Groups resource type
findings.body: getResourceName (around line 332) only special-cases USERS.getType() and falls through to resource.getDisplayName() for everything else. With the new GROUPS resource type the all-groups resource will report its raw name 'Groups' (or whatever getDisplayName returns on top of that), and per-group resources will report their UUID name (because individual group resources are created with name = group.getId() and no displayName is set). It should mirror the Users branch and return 'All groups' / the resolved GroupModel.getName() for the new resource type so error messages, evaluation logs and admin UIs show meaningful labels.

findings.title: Stray double semicolon on the topGroup field initializer
findings.body: Line 68 declares `private final GroupRepresentation topGroup = new GroupRepresentation();;` with two semicolons. It compiles but is a typo worth cleaning up since the rest of the file uses single semicolons consistently.

findings.title: testManageGroupMembership does not verify that joinGroup actually linked the user
findings.body: The last action of testManageGroupMembership (line 306) is `realmAdminClient.realm(realm.getName()).users().get(bobId).joinGroup(topGroup.getId());` without any assertion or follow-up read. The test only distinguishes 'threw' from 'returned cleanly', but if the implementation silently returned a non-error response (e.g. a 404 swallowed by the admin client) the test would still pass even though Bob was never actually joined to topGroup. Add an explicit assertion that lists Bob's group memberships afterwards and contains topGroup.getId().
